title: Processing free literals preserves a variable's non-negating assignment
statement: Let $\ell$ be a literal with variable $v$ and negation flag $b$, let $\rho_0$ and $\sigma$ be restrictions on $n$ variables, and let $\mathit{lits}$ be a list of literals (each tagged with its position index in the clause) run against a decision-tree path. Suppose that every literal in $\mathit{lits}$ whose variable is $v$ is equal to $\ell$, and that $\sigma$ does not already assign $v$ the fixed value $b$, i.e. $\sigma(v) \neq \mathrm{some}\,b$. Then the restriction $\sigma'$ obtained as the $\sigma$-component of processing $\mathit{lits}$ against the path starting from $\rho_0$ and $\sigma$ still does not assign $v$ the value $b$, i.e. $\sigma'(v) \neq \mathrm{some}\,b$.
hypotheses_covered: every literal in the list sharing l's variable equals l
the output σ-component evaluated at l.var
replaced:
If no literal in the input list shares $l$'s variable except $l$ itself, and the initial
$\sigma$ at $l.\mathrm{var}$ is not $\mathrm{some}\ l.\mathrm{neg}$, then after
\texttt{SwitchingLemma2.processClauseLits} the $\sigma$ output at $l.\mathrm{var}$ is still
not $\mathrm{some}\ l.\mathrm{neg}$.
